definitions.gloss: utility knife; box cutter; craft knife
definitions.explanation: A retractable-blade cutting tool with snap-off segments. Extremely common in Japanese offices, schools, and households.

examples.japanese: カッターナイフ⟦で→で：00502_de⟧⟦{段|だん}ボール→段ボール：18885_danbooru⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{切|き}った→切る：02693_kiru⟧。
examples.english: I cut the cardboard with a utility knife.

examples.english: When using a utility knife in craft class, please follow the teacher's instructions.

notes:
A Japanese-English compound (wasei-eigo) combining "cutter" and "knife." In English this tool is typically called a utility knife, box cutter, or craft knife. In Japan, カッターナイフ (or simply ⟦カッター→カッター：24215_kattaa⟧) is a standard school and office supply found in virtually every stationery shop.

The snap-off blade design was invented by the Japanese company OLFA in 1956 and became a global standard.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- カッターナイフ⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{刃|は}→刃：09865_ha⟧: utility knife blade
- カッターナイフ⟦で→で：00502_de⟧⟦{切|き}る→切る：02693_kiru⟧: to cut with a utility knife
- カッターナイフ⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{使|つか}う→使う：00473_tsukau⟧: to use a utility knife
- {替|か}え⟦{刃|は}→刃：09865_ha⟧: replacement blade

SIMILAR WORDS:
- ⟦カッター→カッター：24215_kattaa⟧: cutter — the everyday short form; same tool
- ⟦はさみ→はさみ：00702_hasami⟧: scissors — for cutting paper and fabric with two blades
- ⟦ナイフ→ナイフ：01039_naifu⟧: knife — general term for any knife
